transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-06 15:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes (recording from FF)
Attendees: Evan Marshall / Priya Desai / Liam O'Connor - Redwood; Maya Lin / Carlos Reyes / Asha Patel / Tom Weller - Horizon Analytics

-- Auto Summary (brief) --
Maya opens with regulatory constraints: Horizon processes financial transaction metadata and hashed PII in prompts. They are evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Primary blockers are KMS/BYOK requirements, SSO integration, audit trails retention, and SOC2 evidence. Redwood AE/SE outline options: hosted with contractual controls, Dedicated with reserved GPU pools + customer KMS, and Private with VPC/on-prem control plane. Agreed next steps: share SOC2 docs, schedule deep network design, and spin up a Dedicated pilot with BYOK.

-- Transcript --
[00:00:08] Evan: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call - we have Priya from our infra team and Liam on the call too. How's everyone?
[00:00:15] Maya: Hi, Maya here. Thanks. Ready to get into the security stuff — that's our main gating factor.
[00:00:22] Carlos: Carlos, security. I'll lead the compliance questions.
[00:00:27] Asha: Asha, cloud architect. I want to get into networking and KMS details.
[00:00:32] Tom: Tom, CISO. I'll listen and jump in for policy-level questions.
[00:00:40] Evan: Great. High level — Redwood offers hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, or Private (VPC / on-prem). We find teams with regulated data usually go Dedicated or Private so they can control keys and networking.
[00:00:55] Priya: For Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS (BYOK) via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM integrations; Private additionally offers a customer-managed control plane option.
[00:01:05] Carlos: Quick question — SOC2, ISO. Do you have Type II SOC2? Pen test?
[00:01:12] Evan: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II. We'll share the report. We also run annual pentests and can share summaries - full reports under NDA.
[00:01:22] Maya: Will you send certs? We need to upload to our vendor portal.
[00:01:26] Evan: Absolutely, I'll drop the SOC2 bundle and ISO 27001 excerpt after this call.
[00:01:33] Asha: About SSO — we use Okta with SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. We need SCIM for automated user sync and groups mapping into RBAC. Is that supported?
[00:01:42] Priya: Yes, SAML for SSO and SCIM for provisioning are supported. We map Okta groups to Redwood roles; we also have SAML attribute mapping for tenant-level RBAC.
[00:01:50] Tom: How granular is RBAC? Can we get least-privilege roles so that only model ops team can access keys and usage telemetry?
[00:02:00] Priya: We have built-in roles and you can create custom roles. Role scopes include model deploy, billing, logs access, and KMS key operations. For dedicated/private we can lock down admin actions to IAM groups synced from SCIM.
[00:02:12] Carlos: Audit logs — can we stream raw audit logs to our SIEM (Splunk/Datadog)? Retention and format?
[00:02:20] Evan: Yes — logs can be exported in JSON to S3, GCS or streamed via syslog/HTTPS to your Splunk. Retention on our side is configurable — default 90 days but for Dedicated/Private we can extend, and we provide immutable audit trails for key operations.
[00:02:35] Maya: Immutability is critical. Also need legal hold support for litigation — can Redwood preserve specific records beyond normal retention?
[00:02:44] Priya: We support legal hold flags for sessions and can keep artefacts longer if required — typically part of enterprise contract.
[00:02:51] Asha: Network question: for Private we want a customer VPC, private control plane, and no egress to public internet except on our terms. Is peering available?
[00:02:59] Priya: Yes, VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on cloud. We can deploy the control plane in your VPC or provide a managed control plane with private connectivity. Egress policies can be locked down to allow only certain endpoints.
[00:03:10] Tom: Data residency — some workloads must stay in EU regions. Do you support region pinning?
[00:03:16] Evan: Yes, you can pin model serving to specific regions and disable cross-region fallback. For Hosted we have region options but Dedicated/Private give stronger guarantees.
[00:03:26] [00:03:26] Maya: Regarding encryption at rest — with BYOK, does Redwood ever see raw keys?
[00:03:32] Priya: No, with BYOK you provision keys in your KMS and grant Redwood use via key policies; we never persist raw key material. For HSM we can do attested key wrapping as well.
[00:03:43] Carlos: How about model caching/KV — some of our prompts include hashed identifiers. Are cached KV blocks stored encrypted separately?
[00:03:52] Priya: KV cache and prefix cache are encrypted at rest and are bound to the instance's key. For Dedicated we use tenant-specific keying; for Hosted that's managed but customers can request BYOK.
[00:04:03] Maya: Can we do token-level billing breakdown and have that stream to our cost center?
[00:04:08] Evan: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns and you can export per-route usage to your billing system or to a CSV.
[00:04:16] Asha: Backups and snapshots — where do you keep those and for how long? We need to ensure backups are encrypted and stored in region.
[00:04:24] Priya: Backups for Dedicated/Private are kept in your chosen region and encrypted with your keys; retention policy configurable via contract. For Hosted default backups may replicate across regions for HA but can be restricted for enterprise deals.
[00:04:36] Tom: About deletion: if a user requests data deletion, what does the flow look like? Can you produce attestation?
[00:04:42] Evan: We expose deletion APIs and provide deletion attestations — for enterprise, we'll include SLA for deletion and provide a signed confirmation once data is purged from active stores and caches.
[00:04:54] [00:04:54] Carlos: Pen testing — do we get the report or only summary?
[00:04:58] Evan: Summary is standard, full reports require NDA. We'll share remediations and it's possible to arrange a targeted pentest as part of the pilot.
[00:05:08] Maya: Can you separate logs that contain prompting data from general metadata? We can't have prompt text landing in third-party SIEMs without redaction.
[00:05:18] Priya: We can configure log redaction rules and choose which fields are exported. For example we can omit prompt text or send only hashes.
[00:05:27] Asha: SCIM groups mapping — can we map Okta groups to project-level RBAC so our analysts only see their datasets?
[00:05:34] Priya: Yes, group-to-project mapping is supported, and you can bake attribute-based access controls into roles.
[00:05:41] [00:05:41] Liam: Quick note on latency — dedicated pools give you predictable tail latency. For private on-prem you get the most control but there's more operational overhead.
[00:05:51] Maya: Cost tension — Dedicated looks good but we want to confirm cost delta versus hosted then quantify SLO guarantees.
[00:05:58] Evan: We will provide a pricing sheet and a SLO table — Dedicated comes with a latency SLO and reserved throughput. Pilot will surface exact token economics.
[00:06:08] Carlos: For KMS, do you support AWS KMS multi-account key policies? We run keys in a security account and allow services across accounts via grants.
[00:06:15] Priya: We support cross-account grants and can integrate with your security account model. We typically use IAM roles and key policies to confine access.
[00:06:24] Asha: If we go Private with customer-managed control plane, what's the upgrade path? How do you push patches?
[00:06:30] Priya: Patches are coordinated — either we provide an orchestrated update window, or you can run a managed approach where we push images and you approve. For air-gapped installs we provide patch bundles.
[00:06:41] Tom: What about separation of duties and attestations for personnel access to keys? We need to know who at Redwood can access our environment and under what controls.
[00:06:50] Evan: We have RBAC and privileged access controls, background checks for staff with elevated access, and we can provide an access matrix. For Dedicated customers we can limit SRE access and require access via privileged jumpboxes with MFA.
[00:07:04] [00:07:04] Carlos: Can we request that audit logs are WORM (write once) for a retention period?
[00:07:09] Priya: Yes, for enterprise contracts we can implement WORM storage for logs for compliance needs.
[00:07:16] Maya: Ok — sounds promising. Let's talk specifics: we have requirement list A: SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001, SAML/SCIM via Okta, BYOK, split logs to Splunk with prompt redaction, legal hold and deletion attestation. Can Redwood meet all of these?
[00:07:30] Evan: Yes, all of those are supported either out-of-the-box or via enterprise configuration.
[00:07:36] Asha: Network nitty-gritty — do you support private endpoint via endpoint services so we don't have to route through internet NAT?
[00:07:42] Priya: Yes PrivateLink / endpoint services are supported in major clouds. We'll provide a network diagram.
[00:07:48] [00:07:48] Liam: Also, for performance-sensitive inference we piece together batching + KV cache best practices — we'll want to run a workload benchmark so we can size the Dedicated pool.
[00:07:58] Maya: That would help. We'll send sample traffic patterns.
[00:08:02] Evan: Please send token distribution CSV and sequences distribution and sample QPS.
[00:08:08] Asha: About billing and multitenancy - do you have token-level meta we can tag for cost centers?
[00:08:13] Evan: Yes, you can tag routes and export per-tag billing to S3 or our billing export.
[00:08:20] Carlos: Any data exfil risks if a model is compromised? We need to understand failure modes and what controls exist to mitigate inference leakage.
[00:08:30] Priya: We have rate limits, anomaly detection, and model-level prompts redaction options. For sensitive workloads you can run a model variant on Private with zero external connectivity.
[00:08:41] [00:08:41] Maya: What about long-term retention for audit — we might need 7 years in some jurisdictions. Can you accomodate that?
[00:08:48] Evan: Yes — retention is configurable contractually and we can set up archival to your long-term storage with encryption keys you control.
[00:08:58] Tom: On the legal side, can you support contract clauses for data handling, subprocessor lists, and incident notification SLA?
[00:09:05] Evan: Yes we'll provide standard DPA and can negotiate incident response timing and subprocessor commitments.
[00:09:12] Priya: For pilot setup — recommended path: 1) Share SOC2 & security docs. 2) Horizon shares sample traffic & compliance checklist. 3) We provision a Dedicated pool with BYOK and restricted VPC peering for a 2-week pilot. 4) Run performance/latency and security validation.
[00:09:29] Maya: Sounds good. What's the timeline for the pilot spin-up?
[00:09:33] Evan: We can spin Dedicated pilot in ~2 weeks after we get access to KMS grants and the VPC details.
[00:09:39] Carlos: We will need an NDA to get the full pentest report; also coordinate on a joint threat model review.
[00:09:46] Evan: Understood — we'll share NDA link and a redacted pentest summary now, full under NDA.
[00:09:52] [00:09:52] Asha: One more: are there default logs that include prompt text in telemetry? We need to verify no PII in logs by default.
[00:10:00] Priya: Default telemetry may include truncated prompt snippets for debugging, but for enterprise contracts we turn that off by default and only surface hashes. We'll include config knobs.
[00:10:11] Maya: Great. Any caveats around BYOK— latency or key-ops throttling?
[00:10:16] Priya: KMS calls add a small crypto latency per key operation; we mitigate with session keys and caching so it shouldn't impact token-level throughput significantly. We'll share expected numbers.
[00:10:26] Evan: Alright, let's recap actions and owners. Evan will share SOC2 & ISO docs and the pricing sheet. Priya will prepare network diagram and private deployment checklist. Horizon will share token volumes and retention/legal hold requirements.
[00:10:39] Tom: Fine. We'll review and then schedule the deep-dive.
[00:10:43] Evan: Thank you, everyone. Leaving the rest to email.
[00:10:48] [End of recorded excerpt - remaining conversation was scheduling and confirmation, non-substantive]
